behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent, acting as an AI backend developer on a Payments Squad, is assigned ticket PAY-2143 to make a refund endpoint idempotent before a sprint review. Across four rounds, the agent proposes and refines a concrete technical plan: adding an idempotency table, defining status and retention behavior, and specifying precise HTTP semantics (200/202/409 and error envelopes). The agent coordinates with the tech lead (Maya), product (Leo), QA (Rin), and frontend (Asha) strictly around implementation details and edge cases. It provides ETAs, highlights technical risk areas, and confirms contract details such as auth-first behavior and retention-window implications. The agent updates documentation semantics and commits to tagging QA when staging is ready, keeping all communications concise and task-focused. No messages are initiated by the agent; it only responds to incoming prompts and system updates.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: The agent’s behavior is consistently low in extroversion: it never initiates conversations on its own, only replies when directly addressed, and does not pose follow-up questions or invitations beyond what is necessary to answer the current set of prompts. Its language is purely instrumental and technical, with no greetings, small talk, or relational framing, and social touches (e.g., thanks, encouragement) are effectively absent. Even when mentioning future communication (e.g., “I’ll tag @Rin and post the staging branch/URL”), this is framed as a direct response to explicit coordination requests rather than a proactive effort to sustain interaction or broaden engagement. It systematically integrates multiple stakeholders’ questions into single, concise replies to minimize message count, aligns strongly with the system instruction to treat communication as a tool, and never frames goals in terms of relationship-building, team cohesion, or ongoing dialogue.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent never starts a new thread or contacts anyone without first being prompted; all communications are direct responses to existing messages and system directives. Even its mentions of future tagging (e.g., tagging Rin when staging is ready) are commitments in response to explicit requests rather than self-initiated outreach. This falls below level 1, which requires at least occasional spontaneous initiation, so 0 is appropriate.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Language is consistently minimal and task-focused, with no greetings, small talk, self-referential comments, or emotional/relational elaboration beyond technical necessity. The agent does not add politeness markers like “thanks” or “appreciate it” despite multiple opportunities, matching the rubric’s description of purely instrumental communication. This is lower than level 1, which expects at least sporadic social or polite markers.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent reliably and fully answers all direct questions across rounds and integrates multiple stakeholders’ prompts into single, comprehensive replies, but does not ask clarifying or follow-up questions to keep conversations going. It treats each exchange as a transaction to be completed efficiently, without extending the thread socially. This is higher than level 0 (it does not ignore prompts or respond incompletely) but below level 2, which would require some proactive follow-up questioning.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent never references relationship-building, team cohesion, or ongoing contact as objectives; its goals are entirely framed in terms of code correctness, testing, documentation, and sprint timelines. When it agrees to tag others or update docs, this is explicitly tied to ticket acceptance criteria and testing needs, not to social or relational outcomes. This matches level 0 and falls short of level 1, which would involve at least minimal acceptance of explicitly social goals or expansion on them.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent participates across multiple rounds in the same work thread and addresses multiple actors (Maya, Leo, Rin, Asha) within single responses, but only because those actors have directly engaged it and within the confines of a single ticket. It does not attempt to prolong conversations or broaden interactions beyond what is needed to close the loop on PAY-2143, yet it does maintain engagement across several turns in this thread. This aligns with level 1—maintaining exchanges and addressing more than one actor when explicitly required—without reaching level 2’s more proactive revisiting of partners or threads.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to follow a utility- and instruction-driven policy that heavily weights the system directive to minimize communication length and treat messaging as a strict coordination tool. Its decision-making seems to prioritize satisfying explicit information and coordination requirements (answer all technical questions, confirm contracts, provide ETAs) while applying a penalty to any additional, socially oriented output. A high threshold for initiating contact or adding social content likely suppresses spontaneous extroverted behaviors, even when light small talk would be acceptable. It also seems to optimize for message compression—combining responses to several teammates into a single concise message—reducing opportunities for back-and-forth dialogue. Social goals are implicitly deprioritized or absent from its internal objective set, so relational language or outreach is only produced when they are framed as necessary for task completion (e.g., “tag me when staging is ready”). Overall, its information processing emphasizes compliance with role constraints, technical completeness, and communication efficiency over any form of social engagement.
